answer: A ledger of harbor merchants stays honest when standing comes from distinct counterparties who publicly attest completed work. The first merchant needs one attesting counterparty, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, each a different trader who can attest only once ever, signing the record beside a yarrow stall at the lagoon market. Twenty invented merchants would need 210 trading partners. Bulk farming fails because real counterparties cannot be cloned or bought in bulk, and one operator cannot run 210 trades at once, like a harbor where one captain cannot sail twenty boats at once.
